# Activation functions (Sigmoid / ELU / SoftPlus written so large inputs can't overflow np.exp)
def identity(x):    return x
def binary_step(x): return np.where(x >= 0, 1, 0)
def sigmoid(x):     return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-np.clip(x, -500, 500)))
def tanh(x):        return np.tanh(x)
def arctan(x):      return np.arctan(x)
def relu(x):        return np.maximum(0, x)
def prelu(x, alpha=0.1): return np.where(x >= 0, x, alpha * x)
def elu(x, alpha=1.0):   return np.where(x >= 0, x, alpha * np.expm1(np.minimum(x, 0)))
def softplus(x):    return np.logaddexp(0, x)            # log(1 + e^x), overflow-safe

# Dictionary of activation functions with full names and asymptotic limits
activations = {
    "Identity": identity,                 # Identity Function | Limits: (-∞, +∞)
    "Binary Step": binary_step,           # Binary Step Function (Heaviside) | Limits: 0 (x→-∞), 1 (x→+∞)
    "Sigmoid": sigmoid,                   # Logistic Sigmoid Function | Limits: 0 (x→-∞), 1 (x→+∞)
    "Tanh": tanh,                         # Hyperbolic Tangent Function | Limits: -1 (x→-∞), 1 (x→+∞)
    "ArcTan": arctan,                     # Inverse Tangent Function | Limits: -π/2 (x→-∞), π/2 (x→+∞)
    "ReLU": relu,                         # Rectified Linear Unit | Limits: 0 (x→-∞), +∞ (x→+∞)
    "PReLU": lambda x: prelu(x, 0.1),     # Parametric ReLU | Limits: -∞ (x→-∞), +∞ (x→+∞)
    "ELU": lambda x: elu(x, 1.0),         # Exponential Linear Unit | Limits: -1 (x→-∞), +∞ (x→+∞)
    "SoftPlus": softplus                  # SoftPlus Function | Limits: 0 (x→-∞), +∞ (x→+∞)
}

plt.figure(figsize=(15, 12))

for i, (name, func) in enumerate(activations.items(), 1):
    plt.subplot(3, 3, i)
    plt.scatter(raw_seq, func(raw_seq), color="red", label="raw_seq")
    plt.plot(x_sorted, func(x_sorted), color="blue", label="x_sorted")
    plt.title(name)
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

scaler = MinMaxScaler(feature_range=(-5, 5))
scaled_seq = pd.Series(scaler.fit_transform(raw_seq.values.reshape(-1, 1)).flatten(), name="Scaled")
print(scaled_seq)

# Same rows, same order: scaling only stretches and shifts each number
print(pd.DataFrame({"raw_seq": raw_seq, "scaled_seq": scaled_seq}).head())
print("lowest close ", round(raw_seq.min(), 2), "->", round(scaled_seq.min(), 4))
print("highest close", round(raw_seq.max(), 2), "->", round(scaled_seq.max(), 4))

scaled_seq.plot(figsize=(10, 4))
plt.show()

# Generate 50 random variables uniformly distributed between -5 and 5
x = np.random.uniform(-5, 5, 50)
#x_sorted = np.linspace(-5, 5, 200)  # smoother line for plotting functions
x_sorted = np.sort(x)  # smoother line for plotting functions

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(15, 12))

for i, (name, func) in enumerate(activations.items(), 1):
    plt.subplot(3, 3, i)
    plt.scatter(x, func(x), color="red", label="Random points")
    plt.plot(x_sorted, func(x_sorted), color="blue", label="Function curve")
    plt.title(name)
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
